description: Calls an LLM using a named prompt from PGC_Prompt. Resolves template variables from local_state into the prompt. Also injects PGC_SystemContext rows where inject_for includes the prompt intent_category. Runs the 2-attempt validation/correction loop. Writes the validated output object to output_key.

input_contract.description: intent_category key into PGC_Prompt — identifies which prompt to use
local_state key where the validated LLM output object is written

Additional keys in input (beyond prompt) become {{key}} substitution variables in the prompt text. Key name must match the placeholder exactly — snake_case user_input matches {{user_input}}, NOT {{userInput}}. user_input is also sent as the LLM's human/user message.
Routing token — defaults to "next"
Routing token — use "cancel" for unrecoverable failures

output_contract.description: The validated LLM output object written to local_state[output_key]

description: Runs a pure synchronous JS IIFE expression via acorn AST gate + vm.runInNewContext(200ms timeout). Two sandbox bindings: (1) items — the resolved value of input_key from local_state. (2) local_state — the full workflow state object; use local_state.key_name to read any prior step output. Expression must return the output value. No async, no I/O, no Node globals. Use for data transforms, score tallies, filter operations, loop state mutations, boolean flag computation.

input_contract.description: Synchronous JS IIFE. items = resolved input_key value. local_state = full workflow state. Must return output value. Example: "(function(){ return items.map(function(t){ return Object.assign({}, t, { domain: local_state.proposed_scaffold.domain }); }); })()"
Optional dot-path into local_state resolving to the input value bound as 'items'. Omit when the expression reads everything it needs directly from local_state.
Dot-path where the result is written to local_state. Comma-separate multiple keys (e.g. "a,b,c") to destructure an object return value into multiple top-level local_state keys simultaneously.
Routing token — supports step:N for backward loops

output_contract.description: Result of the expression written to local_state[output_key]

description: Suspends workflow execution and presents a dialog to the user. Execution resumes when the user clicks an option button. Gate types: confirm (read message, click button — output_key written when context_key also present), edit_list (review and remove items), text_input (type free text in an inline Slack input block — output_key always written on submit), review_object (review key-value summary), choice (single-select with lettered buttons A/B/C, per-option description lines — output_key written with selected value; when a choice option carries a modal descriptor, the typed modal text is written to the option's own output_key if declared, or to the step-level output_key if not), followup_prompt (shows a message with an "Ask follow-up" button that opens a free-text modal — no output_key written by the gate itself; the follow-up text is handled by the EXP tier). Each option has its own on_select routing token. special_buttons appear as action buttons only — never in description lists — and support modal descriptors for overlay text input. Optional reveal field: add { button_label, content } to any gate_type to render a single inline task_card above the gate buttons — does NOT advance the workflow (gate stays suspended). Optional reveals field: array version of reveal — one task_card per entry (e.g. one per table). Each entry is { button_label, content }. Supports an inline array or a {{template}} reference to a local_state array.

input_contract.description: confirm | edit_list | text_input | review_object | choice | followup_prompt
Message shown to user — supports {{template}} substitution
Dot-path into local_state for the data shown in the dialog. Required for edit_list and review_object. Optional for confirm — when present, the selected action value is written to output_key.

Array of option objects — must include at least one with action/value: "cancel" in either options or special_buttons. Shape varies by gate_type: confirm/edit_list/review_object use { label, action, on_select }; choice uses { value, label, description, on_select } where value is the machine identifier written to output_key, label is the short button text (e.g. "A", "B"), and description is the explanatory sentence displayed above the buttons. Any option may carry a modal descriptor: { title, input_label, placeholder, multiline } — clicking the button opens a Slack overlay modal; the typed value is written to the option's own output_key if declared, otherwise to the step-level output_key on submit. Any option in a choice gate may carry iterator: '<local_state_key>' — at runtime buildDialog expands it into one button per item in localState[iterator], resolving label/value/description tokens against each item. Use instead of a preceding js_transform when buttons come from a variable-length array. Only one option per gate should carry iterator; include a separate Cancel option without it.

Optional array of action buttons that appear after options buttons but are never rendered in description_list or content fields. Same shape as options per gate_type. Use for Cancel, Other, or modal-trigger buttons that should not appear in the displayed option list. Supports modal descriptor: { title, input_label, placeholder, multiline } — clicking opens a Slack overlay modal; typed value is written to output_key on submit, overriding the button value. The cancel obligation can be satisfied here instead of in options.
text_input gate only — short label shown above the inline Slack input element. Defaults to "Your input". Keep concise (2-5 words). The full instructions go in message_template.

For text_input: local_state key where the typed value is written on submit. For confirm with context_key: local_state key where the selected action value is written. For choice: local_state key where the selected option.value is written — when the option carries a modal descriptor, the modal typed text (inputValue) is written instead of the button value.
Default routing when no on_select override applies
Routing on gate execution error — not user cancellation

Optional single task_card block shown inline above the gate buttons. Composable with any gate_type. Shape: { button_label: string, content: string }. Does NOT advance the workflow — the gate stays suspended. content supports {{template}} substitution resolved at suspension time. Both button_label and content must be non-empty strings. Use reveals (array) instead when you need one card per data item.

Array version of reveal — renders one task_card per entry (e.g. one per table). Each entry is { button_label: string, content: string }. Supports an inline JSON array or a {{template}} reference to a local_state array of {button_label, content} objects. Use instead of reveal when the number of cards is determined at runtime. Does NOT advance the workflow — gate stays suspended.

description: Creates a physical PostgreSQL table via SERV-Schema createTable. Also registers the table in PGC_Schema and PGC_TableMap. Used inside iterators driven by a tables array from an LLM call.

input_contract.description: Full table definition object — tableName, target, columns, foreignKeys, constraints, triggers. May be "{{item}}" inside an iterator.
Routing token

description: Inserts a single row into any PGC or PGD table. Table must be registered in PGC_TableMap with allow_insert: true. Returns the inserted row including generated id.

input_contract.description: Table name — must be registered in PGC_TableMap
Row object — system columns (id, created_at, updated_at) are populated automatically. Supports {{template}} — a template resolving to a full object is passed as the row directly.
local_state key where the inserted row object is written
Routing token
Routing token

output_contract.description: The inserted row including populated id

description: Reads rows from a PGC or PGD table with optional filters, ordering, and limit. Writes the rows array to output_key. Empty result (no matching rows) is not an error — returns an empty array.

input_contract.description: Table name — must be registered in PGC_TableMap
Array of { column, op, value } filter objects. Ops: eq, neq, gt, gte, lt, lte, like, in, is_null, not_null
{ column, direction } — direction is "asc" or "desc"
Maximum number of rows to return
local_state key where the rows array is written
Routing token
Routing token

output_contract.description: Array of row objects written directly to local_state[output_key]. NOT wrapped in a {rows:[...]} envelope. Use {{output_key.length}} to count results, never {{output_key.rows.length}}.

description: Updates rows in a PGC or PGD table matching the given filters. Filters must be non-empty — unfiltered mass updates are rejected. Returns updatedCount and updated rows.

input_contract.description: Table name — must be registered in PGC_TableMap with allow_update: true
Non-empty array of { column, op, value } filter objects — must scope to specific rows. Ops: eq, neq, gt, gte, lt, lte, like, in, is_null, not_null
Object of column → new value pairs
local_state key where { tableName, updatedCount, rows } is written
Routing token
Routing token

description: Deletes rows from a PGC or PGD table matching the given filters. Filters must be non-empty — unfiltered mass deletes are rejected. Best practice: precede with serv_query + human_gate confirm so the user confirms which records are deleted.

input_contract.description: Table name — must be registered in PGC_TableMap with allow_delete: true
Non-empty array of { column, op, value } filter objects — must scope to specific rows. Ops: eq, neq, gt, gte, lt, lte, like, in, is_null, not_null
Routing token
Routing token

description: Lists assembled entities via SERV-Entity listEntities. Returns root columns plus jsonb_agg child arrays. Use instead of serv_query for domains with child tables (e.g. recipes with ingredients and steps).

input_contract.description: Entity name matching PGC_EntitySchema.entity_name — e.g. "Recipe"
Array of { column, op, value } filter objects. Ops: eq, neq, gt, gte, lt, lte, like, in, is_null, not_null applied to the root table
Maximum number of entities to return
local_state key where the entities array is written
Routing token
Routing token

output_contract.description: Array of assembled entity objects — root columns plus child arrays keyed by aggregation outputKey

description: Fetches one assembled entity by id via SERV-Entity getEntity. Returns root columns plus child arrays. Use for id-based single-record lookup.

input_contract.description: Entity name matching PGC_EntitySchema.entity_name — e.g. "Recipe"
Primary key id of the root entity row
local_state key where the assembled entity object is written
Routing token
Routing token

output_contract.description: Assembled entity object — root columns plus child arrays. Single object, not an array.

description: Loads a full entity schema by reading PGC_EntitySchema for join topology and PGC_Schema for live column definitions. Returns entity_name, root { table, columns }, and children [{ table, alias, fk_column, output_key, columns }]. System and FK columns excluded. Use before llm_call steps that need the schema to parse or validate entity input.

input_contract.description: Entity name matching PGC_EntitySchema.entity_name — e.g. "Recipe". Supports {{template}} substitution.
local_state key where the full schema object is written
Routing token
Routing token

output_contract.description: { entity_name, description, root: { table, columns: [{name,type}] }, children: [{ table, alias, fk_column, output_key, columns: [{name,type}] }] }

description: Inserts a multi-level entity into its PGD tables in topological order. Derives parent-child relationships from the entity schema (output of serv_entity_schema). Handles n-level hierarchies by threading FK IDs between levels (index-based matching) and self-referential tables via two-pass insert+update. Use after parse_entity_input has produced a parsed_entity.

input_contract.description: Full entity schema object from serv_entity_schema output ({{full_entity_schema}}). Must contain root.table and children array with parent/fk_column fields.
Parsed entity object from parse_entity_input llm_call ({{parsed_entity}}). Must contain root: {} and children: { <outputKey>: [...] }.
local_state key where the result is written
Routing token
Routing token

output_contract.description: { root_id: number, root_record: object, inserted_counts: { <alias>: number } }

description: Evaluates a template expression against local_state and routes to one of two named steps without performing any I/O or writing to local_state. Truthy: non-empty string, non-zero number, non-null object. Falsy: empty string, "null", "undefined", "0", "false". on_truthy and on_falsy are bare step keys (e.g. "2", "3a") — same rule as all other routing fields.

input_contract.description: {{template}} expression resolved against local_state — e.g. "{{quiz_done}}". Must resolve to a scalar truthy/falsy value. For complex conditions, pre-compute a boolean flag in a prior js_transform.
Bare step key to jump to when expression is truthy (e.g. "2", "3a"). Same format as all other routing fields.
Bare step key to jump to when expression is falsy (e.g. "3", "4b"). Same format as all other routing fields.

description: Dry-runs a workflow step array through three validation levels without calling real services. Level 1: static analysis — routing values, dead targets, missing templates, gate structure. Level 2: path execution using mock_outputs and simulation_paths decision scripts. Level 3: skip-path analysis (advisory). Used by create_workflow to validate generated steps before registration.

input_contract.description: Dot-path into local_state resolving to the steps array to simulate
Dot-path to mock_outputs object — required for Level 2. If absent, runs Level 1 only.
Dot-path to simulation_paths array — required for Level 2. If absent, runs Level 1 only.
local_state key where the SimulateWorkflowResponse object is written
Routing token — taken when all levels pass
Routing token — taken when any level fails. Typically "step:N" to route back to a review gate.

output_contract.description: SimulateWorkflowResponse — { passed, paths_run, paths_passed, paths_failed, static_analysis, path_results, skip_path_warnings }

description: Sends a message to the user via the callback channel (Slack or any UI). The message_template is resolved against local_state. Does not block — fire and forget. No on_failure field — errors are silently discarded. Typically the second-to-last step before end.

input_contract.description: Message text — supports {{template}} substitution from local_state
SQS message type — defaults to HUMAN_NOTIFICATION
Routing token — typically "end" on the final notify step. Only next and end are valid.

description: Executes a single item_step once per element of an array in local_state. Always sequential — one item at a time. Collects results into output_key array after all items complete. execution_mode must always be "sequential". The item_step runs with the parent frame local_state plus the injected item binding.

input_contract.description: Dot-path into local_state resolving to the array to iterate over

Step definition executed once per item. Use {{item}} or {{item.field}} to reference the current element. All parent local_state keys are also readable. Two categories: non-suspending item_steps (serv_schema, serv_insert, serv_update, serv_delete, serv_query, llm_call, js_transform) run inline within a single Lambda invocation. Suspending item_steps (human_gate with gate_type: "choice") suspend the iterator after each item and resume on user response — only gate_type: "choice" is valid inside an iterator. Dynamic options pattern: set "options": "{{item.options}}" on the human_gate item_step — the single-token template resolves to the current item’s options array at runtime, enabling per-item dynamic choice lists built by a prior js_transform step.
Must always be "sequential". Omitting this causes non-sequential execution that exhausts Lambda concurrency on large batches.
local_state key in the PARENT frame where the collected results array is written after all items complete
Routing token after all items complete — defaults to "next"
Routing token if an item_step fails

output_contract.description: Array of outputValue from each item_step execution, written to the parent frame after all items complete

description: Terminal step — marks the workflow run as completed. No input or output fields. No routing fields. Every workflow must have exactly one end step and it must be the last step in the array.

Persists a memory record to PGC_Memory. content_key points to a local_state key containing a plain-text string. scope values support {{template}} substitution. token_estimate is computed automatically as Math.ceil(content.length / 4). Must be the last step after notify. Never fails the workflow run — errors are logged and execution continues.

input_contract.description: episodic | semantic | procedural
JSONB scope object — values support {{template}} substitution. e.g. {"domain": "{{input.domain}}"}
local_state key containing the plain-text content string to persist
Array of string tags for filtering. e.g. ["schema", "design_decision"]
Integer priority — lower = higher priority. Default 5.
Name of the workflow writing this memory (for attribution)
Step key inside the workflow (for attribution)
Routing token — typically "end". Defaults to "end".
